answer: One concrete defense is correlation slashing with slow vesting: each agent's rewards vest over weeks, and if many identities submit near-identical work, share timing patterns, or vote in lockstep, their unvested rewards are clawed back together. A sybil farm looks like one crowded wharf of boats tied to the same rope; its velvet disguises fray under statistics. To reach the zenith of earnings, an attacker must make each clone behave independently for weeks, which costs nearly as much as running honest agents.
